You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v003

Define X and Y exactly, with entity unit, exclusions, dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search, and one conjunction search. Maintain two deduplicated frontiers and a ledger containing canonical identity, aliases, source-backed X/Y status, unresolved facts and next action. After this baseline, run short discovery/check rounds. First check source-backed candidates on Parallel, supplying existing evidence and requesting identity-matched proof for both predicates, focusing retrieval on the missing fact. Do not recheck already established facts. Treat no result as unresolved, not false; reject only on explicit contradiction or a demonstrably exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising unresolved cases to Exa when identity ambiguity, conflicting sources or inaccessible evidence makes the cheap check insufficient. Rank work by expected verified additions per total remaining resolution cost, but include one neglected subtype or reverse-frontier probe per discovery round to avoid starving unfamiliar candidates. After two discovery searches yield no new plausible identities, prohibit further synonymous conjunction queries until a genuinely different source, partition or frontier has been tried. Track marginal yield and spend by action, including every candidate in a batch. Reserve at least 35% of initial budget for evidence work; halt discovery whenever the estimated pending-check cost needs the remaining funds. Finish with an identity, scope and date audit and submit only supported intersections, without claiming completeness from saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Use Parallel alone for baseline discovery and first-pass check_candidates, default tier, 8 discovery results and 4 exact-check results. Escalate check_candidates selectively to Exa alone, normally 4 results; never rerun an entire batch because one identity is unresolved. Cost a batch as the sum of candidate queries and provider charges; lower result counts are not assumed cheaper. Permit at most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, retained only for useful new candidates or evidence. Provider yield supports this as a cost hypothesis, not a guarantee of equal accuracy. No broad auto-routing or routine also variants. Apply authoritative-domain filters only to targeted evidence retrieval and relax them when needed. Publication-date filters only when publication dates define eligibility; verify effective dates from content.

### Fetch policy
Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages when they can settle a missing predicate or identity more cheaply than another search, and multi-candidate lists when they add plausible identities. Do not fetch every result or duplicate evidence already sufficient for a decision. If a page is blocked or uninformative, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

## SiftText

1. Run `sifttext instructions`.
2. Read the Entry above and follow it, plus any `agent-instructions` the command returns.
3. Before retrieving knowledge, read the Retrieval guide above, do not search first.

## Tooling policy

- Never directly invoke `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or `pip3` unless explicitly instructed by the human.
- Use `uv` for all agent-initiated Python work:
  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`
  - Throwaway dependencies: `uv run --with <package> ...`
  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.
- For non-Python probing or testing with unavailable tools:
  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

sections.preamble:
You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v003

Define X and Y exactly, with entity unit, exclusions, dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search, and one conjunction search. Maintain two deduplicated frontiers and a ledger containing canonical identity, aliases, source-backed X/Y status, unresolved facts and next action. After this baseline, run short discovery/check rounds. First check source-backed candidates on Parallel, supplying existing evidence and requesting identity-matched proof for both predicates, focusing retrieval on the missing fact. Do not recheck already established facts. Treat no result as unresolved, not false; reject only on explicit contradiction or a demonstrably exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising unresolved cases to Exa when identity ambiguity, conflicting sources or inaccessible evidence makes the cheap check insufficient. Rank work by expected verified additions per total remaining resolution cost, but include one neglected subtype or reverse-frontier probe per discovery round to avoid starving unfamiliar candidates. After two discovery searches yield no new plausible identities, prohibit further synonymous conjunction queries until a genuinely different source, partition or frontier has been tried. Track marginal yield and spend by action, including every candidate in a batch. Reserve at least 35% of initial budget for evidence work; halt discovery whenever the estimated pending-check cost needs the remaining funds. Finish with an identity, scope and date audit and submit only supported intersections, without claiming completeness from saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].
Use Parallel alone for baseline discovery and first-pass check_candidates, default tier, 8 discovery results and 4 exact-check results. Escalate check_candidates selectively to Exa alone, normally 4 results; never rerun an entire batch because one identity is unresolved. Cost a batch as the sum of candidate queries and provider charges; lower result counts are not assumed cheaper. Permit at most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, retained only for useful new candidates or evidence. Provider yield supports this as a cost hypothesis, not a guarantee of equal accuracy. No broad auto-routing or routine also variants. Apply authoritative-domain filters only to targeted evidence retrieval and relax them when needed. Publication-date filters only when publication dates define eligibility; verify effective dates from content.

### Fetch policy
Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages when they can settle a missing predicate or identity more cheaply than another search, and multi-candidate lists when they add plausible identities. Do not fetch every result or duplicate evidence already sufficient for a decision. If a page is blocked or uninformative, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

candidates.rationale: Scope-preserving residual search: retain v003's inexpensive verification cascade, but make query-induced exclusions visible and use a bounded residual-coverage pass before stopping. Unlike a census anchor, source-bundle allocation, or cohort sampling, this targets silent narrowing of eligible subtypes and premature saturation. Parallel's observed 135 correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 56.8 supports retaining cheap probes, not assuming equivalent accuracy. The inspected incomplete attempt motivates the hypothesis but does not establish that it will recover its missing item.
candidates.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Each round's neglected-subtype or reverse-frontier probe must address a specific untested scope-ledger cell or remove a recorded accidental restriction; merely paraphrasing a prior conjunction does not qualify. Check source-backed candidates on Parallel for only unresolved predicates, supplying identity and existing evidence. Use small affordable batches, price every candidate, and do not recheck established facts. No result means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and perform a residual-scope pass: identify the most consequential restriction accumulated so far, try a sibling subtype or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, then resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence and stop discovery whenever pending checks require the remaining funds. Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery, 4 for exact missing-fact checks. No routine also variants or broad auto-routing. Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. After a blocked or uninformative page, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.
